sources.note: No stress/accent/tone/pitch remarks anywhere in the chapter (a full-text search for stress/accent printed pp.527-567); no Sialum-specific phonology.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1970. The Selepet language within the Finisterre-Huon phylum (New Guinea). PhD thesis, ANU.
sources.note: Stress statements are for Selepet only; Sialum mentioned only historically (Stolz opened the Sialum mission station in 1907).

sources.citation: TransNewGuinea.org, language page 'Sialum' (lexicon from McElhanon & Voorhoeve 1970)
sources.note: Wordlist only (no stress marks); used to confirm Dempwolff's Pon/Keseraua = Sialum.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarström. 2018. The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area: a comprehensive guide, 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.note: per-language documentation listing only: listing only; the chapter's phonology remarks are at proto-TNG level and name none of these languages
sources.venue: The languages and linguistics of the New Guinea area: a comprehensive guide

sources.citation: Suter, Edgar. 2018. Comparative Morphology of the Huon Peninsula Languages (Papua New Guinea). PhD dissertation, Universitaet zu Koeln. viii+331 pp.
sources.note: Nothing on Sialum stress. p.6: 'the only publication that survives is an ethnographic report containing a glossed mythological text (Stolz 1911). My main source for Sialum is McElhanon's survey fieldnotes.' Sialum appears only in object-verb/pronoun paradigms.

sources.citation: Hammarström, Harald & Sebastian Nordhoff. 2012. Online appendix to 'The languages of Melanesia: quantifying the level of coverage'. In N. Evans & M. Klamer (eds), Melanesian languages on the edge of Asia (LD&C Special Publication 5), 13-34. Honolulu: University of Hawai'i Press.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: coverage inventory only: entry lists Dempwolff 1905, Ray 1919, Ross 1995, Smith 1988 only; no stress/tone statement (database of descriptive coverage, not a description)
sources.venue: Melanesian languages on the edge of Asia (LD&C Special Publication 5)

sources.citation: The Rosetta Project. n.d. [uploaded 2010]. Sialum Swadesh List. archive.org item rosettaproject_slw_swadesh-1 (55 items; forms = McElhanon & Voorhoeve 1970 Sialum).
sources.note: Bare 55-item list, no stress or tone marks, no notes: wordlist-only data, not a statement.

sources.citation: Carrington, Lois. 1996. A linguistic bibliography of the New Guinea area. Pacific Linguistics D-90. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: bibliography only: survey/classification works and Osmers' church-language overview (checked held by the project: Sialum only in a mission-history sentence, p. the text); no phonology

sources.citation: Smith, Geoffrey P. 1988. Morobe counting systems. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26 (Pacific Linguistics A-76), 1-132. Canberra: Australian National University. (no. 59 Sialum, p.85)
sources.note: Nothing: nine numeral expressions without stress or tone marks and no phonological remarks; the volume's 'stress' hits are the English verb. A Glottolog ref (listed by Glottolog as an overview) for sial1240 that A named in its glottolog-diff but did not list as a work; recorded here as opened and silent so later passes need not download it.
sources.venue: Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26 (Pacific Linguistics A-76)

sources.citation: Phinnemore, Thomas R. 1985. Ono phonology and morphophonemics. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 22, Pacific Linguistics A-63: 173-214.
sources.note: Describes the sister language Ono (stress-group analysis); Sialum named once as a neighbouring language, nothing about Sialum stress.
sources.venue: Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 22, Pacific Linguistics A-63: 173-214

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1973. Towards a typology of the Finisterre-Huon languages, New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-22. Canberra: ANU.
sources.harvard_location: Divinity School Library (offsite storage), call number - Ask at Circulation (Pamph. folio) BS 354 .Z91
sources.note: Sialum only in the language list (Western Huon family, d.); the phonology section (phonemes, syllable structure, morphophonemics) says nothing about stress for any language.

sources.citation: Hooley, Bruce A. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Morobe District -- New Guinea. In S. A. Wurm & D. C. Laycock (eds), Pacific Linguistic Studies in Honour of Arthur Capell (Pacific Linguistics C-13), 1065-1094. Canberra: Australian National University.
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: No phonology content for Sialum. p.1071: 'Only one language in this Family, Ono, has been described in any detail (Wacke, 1930), although Rev. Stolz learned Sialum and published Bible stories in that language.. The Sialum language has two dialects 95 percent related. Sialum and Nama villages speak the northern dialect and Kwamkwam (Qambu) village the southern dialect.' Nothing on stress/tone anywhere in the chapter.
sources.venue: Pacific Linguistic Studies in Honour of Arthur Capell (Pacific Linguistics C-13)

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. & C. L. Voorhoeve. 1970. The Trans-New Guinea Phylum: Explorations in deep-level genetic relationships (Pacific Linguistics B-16). Canberra: ANU. (Sialum = 'WHF d' in the comparative wordlists; source of the TransNewGuinea.org and Rosetta slw lists.)
sources.note: Section 1.5 'Spelling' (p.16): 'Most of the data used in this study has not yet been phonemicized; the spelling is therefore phonetic and for practical reasons follows Pike 1947'; symbol table segmental only; Sialum forms carry no stress or pitch marks. Wordlist data, no prosodic statement.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1970. A history of linguistic research in the Huon Peninsula, New Guinea. In Wurm & Laycock (eds), Pacific Linguistics C-13: 1179-1208. doi:10.15144/PL-C13.1178
sources.note: No phonology. Historical/classificatory only: Stolz opened Sialum station 1907; 'That Sialum is NAN rather than AN can be determined by a study of a text provided by Stolz (1911:282-6)'; Schmitz/Bodrogi wrongly listed Sialum as Melanesian. Confirms no pre-1970 description beyond Dempwolff/Ray lists and Stolz's text.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1919. The Languages of Northern Papua. Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute 49: 317-341.
sources.note: Classificatory overview; lists 'Kamoka', 'Pong', 'Keseraua', 'Ago' (villages near Cape King William) in the Papuan 'Kai Group' (p.321), evidently from Dempwolff's specimens; no phonology, nothing on stress.
sources.venue: Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute

sources.citation: Neuhauss, Richard. 1911. Deutsch Neu-Guinea. Band I. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer. Kap. 6 'Sprachen und Völkerstämme', pp.118-130 (p.127 = 'Neuhauss 1911, 1:127' of McElhanon 1970).
sources.note: Nothing on stress, accent, tone, syllables or pronunciation of Sialum (or of any named language) in pp.118-130. Language-related content: general Papuan-vs-Melanesian typology (suffixing vs prefixing verbs, richer pronouns), sounds ('das nasale ng'; p.119 'Bei den Vokalen ist es oft schwer zu sagen, ob man a, e oder o schreiben soll, da die Laute ein Mittelding zwischen den europäischen Vokalen bilden. Etwas ganz Gewöhnliches ist die Vertauschung von R und L'), figurative idioms incl. Sialum ones in German only (p.119 '„Die Stirne beißt ihn“, sagt der Sialum-Mann, wenn er ausdrücken will, daß…

sources.citation: Stolz, Michael. 1911. Die Umgebung von Kap Koenig Wilhelm. In Richard Neuhauss (ed.), Deutsch Neu-Guinea, Band III: Beitraege der Missionare Keysser, Stolz, Zahn, Lehner, Bamler, 244-286. Berlin: Dietrich Reimer.
sources.note: Glottolog's Glottolog's most extensive description for Sialum (ethnographic report with a glossed Sialum myth text by the missionary who worked at Sialum from 1907); the only place a remark on Sialum pronunciation/Betonung or accent-marked text could exist in print. Full-view scans exist but were could not be reached by automated download.
sources.venue: Deutsch Neu-Guinea, Band III: Beitraege der Missionare Keysser, Stolz, Zahn, Lehner, Bamler

sources.citation: Dempwolff, Otto. 1905. Beitraege zur Kenntnis der Sprachen von Deutsch-Neuguinea. Mitteilungen des Seminars fuer Orientalische Sprachen zu Berlin VIII, Abt. 1: 182-254. Section II 'Papuasprachen' b) Pon '(Dorf bei Kap Koenig Wilhelm)' p.243, c) Keseraua '(Dorf etwa 5 km von Pon)' pp.243-244, d) Ago '(Dorf bei Festungshuk, suedlich Kap Koenig Wilhelm)' p.245; transcription conventions p.182.
sources.note: No rule for this language. p.182 gives only his marking convention ('Die Betonung pflegte ich oft nicht zu bezeichnen, wenn sie der uns gelaeufigen auf der vorletzten Silbe entsprach'). The Pon and Keseraua wordlists (Kap Koenig Wilhelm = Sialum; forms match McElhanon & Voorhoeve 1970 Sialum: na 'I', yana 'he', denan 'eye', wauwa 'dog', nani 'bird', namu 'breast') carry acute stress marks on many items (ka'sa, ka'mu, we'sap, la'lam, go-so'n, ka'te, u'nu, be'ra, pe'sum, na'ni, ya'ra, sa-xo'-rup, kon-do'-ro, ta'mba; ma'ma, ne-sa'd-na, be-le-ka'm-na, di'-na-na, sa-ga-ra'-na, ke-na'm-na, me-ta'-n…
sources.venue: Mitteilungen des Seminars fuer Orientalische Sprachen zu Berlin VIII, Abt
